brief.summary: A household utilities organizer where one family member keeps every electric, gas, water, trash and internet account for several homes they're responsible for, along with the bills, meter readings, notices and provider contacts.
brief.user: Danielle Okafor, 44, a pharmacist in Columbus who handles the utilities for her own house, her father's house in Zanesville (he moved to assisted living in March and the house is listed for sale), and the small lake cottage she co-owns with her brother. She's organized but not technical, and she opens the app maybe twice a month.
brief.moment: It's Sunday evening. Her father's neighbor just texted a photo of a yellow notice taped to his door: the gas company says the meter can't be read and someone has to give access by Nov 21 or service may be interrupted. Danielle needs to get from her own home's accounts to her father's house, then to the gas account, find the notice the company also emailed, check when the last real reading was, find the account number and the phone line for scheduling meter access, and then go to the cottage's water account to see if the winter shutoff she asked for in October was ever confirmed. brief.data: 3 properties: '4418 Whitlow Ave, Columbus' (her home, 5 accounts), 'Dad's house, 112 Linden St, Zanesville' (4 accounts: AEP Ohio electric, Columbia Gas, City of Zanesville water/sewer, Spectrum internet—marked 'cancel at closing'), 'Lake cottage, Buckeye Lake' (3 accounts: electric, village water, propane delivery from Hartley Fuel). Each account has: account number, holder name (Dad's accounts still under 'Raymond Okafor', Danielle listed as authorized contact), autopay status, last 12 bills with amounts (Dad's gas ran $38–$141/month), meter readings with 'actual' vs 'estimated' flags (Dad's gas has 3 estimated readings in a row since August), saved notices (the Nov 12 'Meter access required' letter, due Nov 21), provider phone numbers and hours, and Danielle's own notes (e.g., 'Realtor has lockbox code 2291'). The cottage water account has an open service request #W-30871 'Seasonal shutoff' submitted Oct 6, status 'Received', no completion date. 2 other open items across properties: a Spectrum equipment return and an AEP budget-billing enrollment for her home.

prompt:
I need the front end for Pilotlight. A household utilities organizer where one family member keeps every electric, gas, water, trash and internet account for several homes they're responsible for, along with the bills, meter readings, notices and provider contacts.

Who's using it: Danielle Okafor, 44, a pharmacist in Columbus who handles the utilities for her own house, her father's house in Zanesville (he moved to assisted living in March and the house is listed for sale), and the small lake cottage she co-owns with her brother. She's organized but not technical, and she opens the app maybe twice a month.

What they're doing right now: It's Sunday evening. Her father's neighbor just texted a photo of a yellow notice taped to his door: the gas company says the meter can't be read and someone has to give access by Nov 21 or service may be interrupted. Danielle needs to get from her own home's accounts to her father's house, then to the gas account, find the notice the company also emailed, check when the last real reading was, find the account number and the phone line for scheduling meter access, and then go to the cottage's water account to see if the winter shutoff she asked for in October was ever confirmed. She keeps losing track of which property she's in, and she wants to be sure she's looking at her father's gas account and not her own.

What's in the system at this point: 3 properties: '4418 Whitlow Ave, Columbus' (her home, 5 accounts), 'Dad's house, 112 Linden St, Zanesville' (4 accounts: AEP Ohio electric, Columbia Gas, City of Zanesville water/sewer, Spectrum internet—marked 'cancel at closing'), 'Lake cottage, Buckeye Lake' (3 accounts: electric, village water, propane delivery from Hartley Fuel). Each account has: account number, holder name (Dad's accounts still under 'Raymond Okafor', Danielle listed as authorized contact), autopay status, last 12 bills with amounts (Dad's gas ran $38–$141/month), meter readings with 'actual' vs 'estimated' flags (Dad's gas has 3 estimated readings in a row since August), saved notices (the Nov 12 'Meter access required' letter, due Nov 21), provider phone numbers and hours, and Danielle's own notes (e.g., 'Realtor has lockbox code 2291'). The cottage water account has an open service request #W-30871 'Seasonal shutoff' submitted Oct 6, status 'Received', no completion date. 2 other open items across properties: a Spectrum equipment return and an AEP budget-billing enrollment for her home.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
